commit: the verbatim commit the record stamps, read from the field commit_stamp names; scripts/step1_b300_summary.py refuses a record whose stamp is not this.
gzip: gzip -9 -n of the raw file (no name or time in the header). sha256_raw and bytes_raw are of the decompressed bytes, sha256_gz and bytes_gz of the file here.
not_a_row: Exploratory records, not harness rows. scripts/step1_b300_summary.py derives its figures from these files and those of step1-b300-2026-09-26/ and nothing else; see rows/exploratory/README.md.
not_copied: The text logs and the server log.
original: the file name the tool wrote, relative to the step-1 output directory of the machine that ran it

server-ba20c49-ragged-c8-run1.json.gz.what: probes/server_frozen_answers.py: all 2,939 recordings streamed through a running verbatim server on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 (model nvidia/nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b, bucket 128, 160 ms, bfloat16, eager encoder step, decoder graphs off) with --padding ragged, word confidence off, the client admitting 8 sessions at once; records every final text and word timing, the server's observed settings and its tick statistics before and after the run. The first of two ragged captures on one server process.

server-ba20c49-ragged-c8-run2.json.gz.what: probes/server_frozen_answers.py: all 2,939 recordings streamed through a running verbatim server on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 (model nvidia/nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b, bucket 128, 160 ms, bfloat16, eager encoder step, decoder graphs off) with --padding ragged, word confidence off, the client admitting 8 sessions at once; records every final text and word timing, the server's observed settings and its tick statistics before and after the run. The second, taken right after the first: ragged against ragged.

scrubbed: scripts/scrub_record_paths.py replaced the absolute paths each record's tool stamped by a placeholder: <checkout>, the verbatim checkout the tool and the server ran from; <home>, the home directory of the user who ran them; <step1-out>, the directory the step-1 tools wrote their records and logs to; <venv>, the Python virtual environment they ran in. A record that names another here by sha256 names the scrubbed one. sha256_as_written and bytes_as_written are the record as its tool wrote it; scrub says what was replaced. A record without them held no path and is as written.
what: Two ragged captures at concurrency 8 on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 (card 3 of its machine) at ba20c49, 2026-09-26, one after the other on one server process, each gzipped whole. Kept apart from step1-a6000-2026-09-26/ so that directory's manifest, and the summary that names it by sha256, stay byte for byte as merged.
